name: Andorra
summary: Andorran law protects children (or parents if there are none) with a reserved quarter of the estate. It is not in the EU. Trusts are not recognised, and only public-interest foundations are allowed. Several points rest on secondary sources only.
reserved_share: About 25 % of the estate, shared among the children or, with no children, the parents (Act 46/2014 on succession; per UINL summary, secondary source).
foreign_law_note: Per a notarial summary, the testator's national law governs the succession, except where close ties to another state exist. Not under the EU Regulation. Not confirmed from the statute.
trust_note: Andorra is not on the HCCH Trusts Convention table, so it is not in force. Advisers report trusts are not recognised in Andorra. Foundations (Law 11/2008) must pursue general-interest or social purposes.
open_questions: Forced share, applicable-law rule and the absence of a trust law come from secondary sources only.
A reported trust law of 2022 could not be confirmed or ruled out.
Andorra statutes were not read at the Official Gazette (bopa.ad).

sources.title: Act 46/2014 on succession to the estates of the deceased
HCCH status table: 1985 Trusts Convention
